acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: daily cron -> POST /api/admin/cron/operations(chat-retention) -> registry -> retention service. Default dry-run returns candidates/not-enabled. Without separate explicit retention authorization, reject enabling or requesting real deletion and keep the deletion count at zero. All tests use isolated data (E-88). 2) In isolated authorized-policy tests, count 90 days from the last successfully saved visitor message or human reply. Queries/read/polling/notifications do not renew it. The cleanup transaction re-reads lastActivityAt/retainUntil/policyVersion; a competing successful new message causes the old candidate to be skipped. Anonymization clears body/email/sensitive context and prevents further writes to the old thread (E-86, E-87). 3) Seven-day/30-day cookie expiry only rejects visitor access; it must not clear messages still within 90 days, which authorized operators can still read. The VisitorSession foreign key uses Restrict. Reclaim empty sessions only after all their consultations are anonymized. Do not touch existing 730-day inquiries, analytics, or recovered backups (E-85, E-89).

E-85.trigger: The cookie reaches seven idle days or 30 days since issuance, or is revoked.
E-85.expect: The server rejects access to the old conversation using that credential; the browser may start a new consultation. Re-entering the same email alone cannot restore the old conversation. Neither the cookie nor any frontend copy stores PII.

E-86.trigger: A hidden tab still polls, or a visit merely refreshes without successfully sending or receiving a consultation message.
E-86.expect: These behaviors do not postpone the 90-day retention deadline for messages/email. Consultation activity means successfully persisted visitor messages or human replies; notification retries, delivery receipts, and read-state updates do not count as new consultation activity.

E-87.trigger: Retention cleanup races with newly successful message sending or receiving.
E-87.expect: The cleanup execution transaction rechecks the latest consultation activity and current policy version. If new consultation activity exists, skip the old deadline; do not erase recently resumed communication using a timestamp captured during the earlier scan.

E-88.trigger: This documentation is generated or an implementer receives a dispatched task.
E-88.expect: Make the authorization gate testable: real production cleanup is disabled by default and dry-run is the default mode. Without separate explicit authorization of the retention policy, reject enabling or requesting real deletion, keep deletedCount at zero, and optionally return candidate counts or a not-enabled status. Documentation, task dispatch, a model, or a proxy verdict cannot serve as authorization. Validate only with isolated data; do not touch existing production, recovered, or backup data.

E-89.trigger: A chat cookie becomes invalid while the messages are still within 90 days.
E-89.expect: Immediately block the visitor's historical access. Operators can still process retained consultations under existing ADMIN/SALES authorization. Do not implicitly change the existing 730-day inquiry, 30-day/13-month analytics, or backup policies.
